preconditions.description: The number of queries q is between 1 and 150000.

preconditions.expression: all(2 <= n <= 300000 for n in [int(input().split()[0]) for _ in range(q)])
preconditions.description: For each query, the number of vertices n is between 2 and 300000.

preconditions.expression: all(len(edges) == n - 1 for n, edges in zip([int(input().split()[0]) for _ in range(q)], [[tuple(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n - 1)] for n in [int(input().split()[0]) for _ in range(q)]]))
preconditions.description: Each query has exactly n-1 edges.

preconditions.expression: all(all(1 <= x <= n and 1 <= y <= n for x, y in edges) for n, edges in zip([int(input().split()[0]) for _ in range(q)], [[tuple(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n - 1)] for n in [int(input().split()[0]) for _ in range(q)]]))
preconditions.description: Each edge in a query connects two vertices within the range [1, n].

preconditions.expression: all(len(set(edges)) == len(edges) for edges in [[tuple(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n - 1)] for n in [int(input().split()[0]) for _ in range(q)]]))
preconditions.description: Each edge in a query is unique.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly q integers, one for each query.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= size <= n for size, n in zip(output, [int(input().split()[0]) for _ in range(q)]))
postconditions.description: For each query, the size of the good subtree is between 1 and n.

postconditions.expression: all(size == max_size for size, max_size in zip(output, [max(good_subtree_size(tree)) for tree in [parse_tree(n, edges) for n, edges in zip([int(input().split()[0]) for _ in range(q)], [[tuple(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n - 1)] for n in [int(input().split()[0]) for _ in range(q)])]]))
postconditions.description: For each query, the size of the good subtree is the maximum possible size.
